title: Detecting Diffusion-generated Images via Dynamic Assembly Forests
key_findings: The proposed Dynamic Assembly Forest (DAF) model achieves competitive performance under standard evaluation protocols with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost compared to deep neural networks.
DAF can be deployed without GPUs, making it a practical substitute for heavyweight DNN models in resource-constrained scenarios.
research_problem: Investigating traditional machine learning models (specifically the deep forest paradigm) as an alternative to heavyweight deep neural networks (CNNs and Transformers) for detecting diffusion-generated images.
usefulness_reason: Directly addresses lightweight detectors for diffusion-generated images by introducing a parameter-efficient, low-computation, non-DNN model (DAF) that can run without a GPU.
